newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kuwait urges clearing of wrecks from northern Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait urges clearing of wrecks from northern Gulf.

text.p: Kuwait urged the Security Council on Wednesday to ensure the removal of sunken vessels, including tankers, from the northern part of the Gulf, now that Iraq was exporting oil under a limited U.N. "oil-for-food" plan.

In a letter to council President Francesco Paolo Fulci of Italy, Kuwaiti U.N. envoy Mohammaed Abulhasan said the resumption of Iraqi exports from the Mina al-Bakr terminal implied an increase in maritime traffic in that area of the Gulf.

"I would like to draw the attention of the Security Council that the concerned waterways contain numerous sunken vessels, tankers and other wrecks, some of which still contain (a) large amount of oil and possibly some unexploded ordnance.

"Since the removal of such vessels and other wrecks has not been commenced as yet, we would like the Security Council to take all necessary measures, in accordance with its responsibilities, to ensure the removal of all objects and vessels that may constitute a hazard to the marine environment and the safety of the navigation of the Gulf."

Abulhasan did not say how many sunken vessels were involved or how they were sunk. But Iran and Iraq fought an eight-year war from 1980 to 1988 and fighting again erupted in the region after Iraq occupied Kuwait in 1990 and was evicted early the following year by a United States-led coalition.
